# Findings: efficiency decomposition, aggregation, and reproducibility

*Generated by `scripts/generate_findings.py` from `final-overrelaxation-efficiency-campaign-379d46d5354be739-20260705T034447066354Z`, `results/findings/` and `ymlab.symbolic`. Do not edit by hand.*

Builds on Michael Elsbernd's Yang–Mills Mass Gap Laboratory (`ymlab`) and its paired overrelaxation campaign (β ∈ [1.5, 2.0, 2.5], seeds [2026, 2027, 2028], lattice [5, 4, 4], 180 measured updates). This is a **finite-lattice computational-methodology** study; nothing here is a statement about the continuum Yang–Mills mass gap.

## 1. Efficiency ratio decomposes into gain × cost

With N_eff = N/(2τ) and η = N_eff/t, the paired ESS/s ratio of a hybrid schedule to Metropolis is

    R = η_OR / η_M = (τ_M / τ_OR) · (t_M / t_OR)

The number of measurements cancels. R > 1 requires the decorrelation gain τ_M/τ_OR to exceed the cost penalty t_OR/t_M. Sympy derives this (`ymlab.symbolic.efficiency_ratio`) and the test-suite checks it against the recorded ESS/s ratios of every pair to 1e-9.

![gain vs cost](../results/figures/findings/gain_vs_cost.png)

**Finding.** Across all 27 paired (β, seed, schedule) conditions the plaquette ratio was between 0.05 and 0.94; 0 exceeded 1. The gain exceeded 1 in 12 of 27 pairs (max 3.11) but the cost penalty was between 2.8 and 8.4. In this configuration the extra overrelaxation sweeps were never repaid in plaquette ESS/s.

![ESS by schedule](../results/figures/findings/ess_by_schedule.png)

## 2. Aggregation rule changes the reported number

"Mean of paired ratios" and "ratio of mean ESS/s" are different statistics (the mean of products is not the product of means). Both are tabulated; gain and cost factor are per-pair means.

| β | schedule | mean gain | mean cost factor | mean of ratios | ratio of means | pair range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5 | M+1OR | 0.93 | 0.357 | 0.333 | 0.281 | 0.08–0.51 |
| 1.5 | M+2OR | 1.08 | 0.217 | 0.234 | 0.207 | 0.13–0.42 |
| 1.5 | M+4OR | 1.02 | 0.122 | 0.124 | 0.114 | 0.09–0.19 |
| 2 | M+1OR | 1.10 | 0.354 | 0.388 | 0.263 | 0.20–0.75 |
| 2 | M+2OR | 1.32 | 0.216 | 0.284 | 0.152 | 0.08–0.67 |
| 2 | M+4OR | 1.44 | 0.121 | 0.175 | 0.103 | 0.05–0.38 |
| 2.5 | M+1OR | 1.30 | 0.347 | 0.454 | 0.404 | 0.20–0.94 |
| 2.5 | M+2OR | 1.04 | 0.212 | 0.221 | 0.227 | 0.17–0.26 |
| 2.5 | M+4OR | 1.13 | 0.119 | 0.134 | 0.133 | 0.09–0.18 |

The two rules differ by up to 86% of the ratio of means in this table. With three seeds per cell, per-pair ratios are widely dispersed and neither summary should be read as more than descriptive.

![aggregation](../results/figures/findings/aggregation_sensitivity.png)

## 3. What is deterministic and what is not

Two published campaigns with the same configuration hash were compared: maximum |Δτ_int| = 0.0e+00, maximum relative ESS/s difference = 3.9% (same machine). τ_int is deterministic; ESS/s inherits wall-clock noise.

![determinism](../results/figures/findings/determinism.png)

## 4. Reproduction on another platform

On Linux x86_64 (Python 3.13.18, NumPy 2.5.3) the published seed-2026 conditions were re-run; the published runs were made on Darwin arm64 (Python 3.9.6, NumPy 2.0.2). The pure-Metropolis chains reproduce the published τ_int to within 2.2e-13; 0 of 9 hybrid chains reproduce it exactly, with local-to-published τ_int ratios between 0.88 and 4.12. Median runtime here was 2.2× the published runtime. The cause of the hybrid divergence was not isolated (platform, library version, and floating-point ordering are all confounded).

The stored data is in `results/findings/`; rerun with `python scripts/reproduction_check.py`.

## 5. Symbolic models (sympy → LaTeX)

`src/ymlab/symbolic.py` models the lattice coupling β = 2N/g², the SU(2) plaquette term 1 − a₀, trace conjugation invariance, N_eff, the efficiency ratio and its break-even, the AR(1) τ_int = (1+φ)/(2(1−φ)), the cosh effective-mass identity, and the Creutz-ratio cancellation of perimeter and constant terms in an area law. Each has a numeric check against the numerical code in `tests/test_symbolic.py`. Illustrations: `ar1_tau`, `area_law_creutz`, `effective_mass_plateau` in `results/figures/findings/`.

## Limits

Three seeds, one lattice shape (5×4×4), SU(2), one observable emphasised (plaquette). The ESS/s ranking is specific to this implementation's Python/NumPy cost structure. Hybrid-chain divergence across platforms is observed, not explained.
